_why: ADR 0067's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The notice that Terrium is not Tellurium lived in two files that both
stay in the repository. Someone who runs `pip install terrium` never
saw either. These five rows are the ways that could silently become
N4 is the one worth reading twice. Disclaiming ('not Tellurium') and
attributing ('runs on libRoadRunner') are different obligations -- the
first is Terrium's own problem, the second is what the licences ask
for. A surface that does only the first looks compliant and is not.

mutations.description: the notice is edited out of CITATION.cff
mutations._note: Citation metadata is what a reference manager ingests, and citation is exactly where credit confusion does its damage.
README and NOTICE stay in the repository; a docstring travels with the installed package. This is the surface that reaches someone who never opens GitHub.
mutations.find: NOT TELLURIUM. Tellurium is a separate, established systems-biology
mutations.replace: Tellurium is a separate, established systems-biology

mutations.description: a missing surface is skipped instead of failing
mutations._note: Deleting the file is the easiest way to pass a checklist. A guard that shrugs at a missing surface rewards exactly that.

mutations.description: the credit requirement is dropped, so a denial without an attribution passes
mutations._note: The distinction the ADR is named for. Saying 'we are not them' while staying silent on 'we are built on their software' satisfies nobody's licence.
mutations.find: if rel in MUST_CREDIT and not _CREDIT_RE.search(text):

mutations.description: the checklist is gutted to a single surface
mutations._note: The floor exists because shortening the list is indistinguishable from passing it.
